solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lamp is a plug-in electrical appliance

explanation.surface: Someone told to seize a chilly household gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a tool that holds things tightly, so as a verb it means to hold firmly, just as grip does.

clue.text: Say a cult transformed injured party

indicators.note: something transformed has changed form, so these letters take on a new order

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone harmed by a sect that has changed them.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is a person hurt or killed in an accident or conflict.

clue.text: Nimble US soldier drowning in beer

indicators.note: something drowning in a liquid is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
GI is the nickname for an American serviceman

explanation.surface: A quick-footed American soldier swamped in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means able to move quickly and easily, the same as nimble.

parts.note: pepper is a common seasoning
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Putting spice on a single sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried Italian-American sausage, often sliced on pizza.

indicators.note: the run of words literally includes the solution inside its own letters, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A traveller's invoice turns out to list a small pet as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerbil is a small burrowing desert mammal of the rodent family, often kept as a pet.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of vellum

explanation.surface: Wood fibres turning up again and again in fine parchment.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber from the elm tree, so it can stand for wood.

clue.text: Trust from worker perhaps covering cover up

indicators.note: one thing covering another wraps around it, so one piece sits outside the other

parts.note: the worker bee; 'perhaps' because a bee is one example of a worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: Faith in an employee who may be hiding a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' looks like one phrase meaning conceal, but cover is the piece and up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe someone is to trust that what they say is true.

indicators.note: one word placed around another encloses it, so the second piece sits inside

parts.note: led is the past tense of lead, to guide
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone was steered around the north ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In advance' reads as meaning beforehand; here 'in' is only a link and advance is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money to someone is to lend it, as with a loan or an advance on wages.

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a position is a post or job

explanation.surface: Someone backing a proposal about work.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition is an idea or plan put forward for consideration, a proposal or suggestion.

clue.text: Captain beginning to skin smoked fish

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of skin
a kipper is a split, salted and smoked herring, a British breakfast staple

explanation.surface: A ship's master starts preparing a smoked fish by removing its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a boat or the leader of a team, an informal synonym for captain.

clue.text: First of all merchants exchange limes or nectarines for other fruit

indicators.note: the first of all the following words means the opening letter of each one in turn

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words in order

explanation.surface: Traders swap their citrus and stone fruit for something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' looks like an anagram signal, but it is just one of the five words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large fruit with sweet flesh, different from the limes and nectarines in the surface, hence 'other'.

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of adult
PE, physical education, is the school subject often called games in Britain

explanation.surface: An instruction to imitate the opening of some grown-up games.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to imitate or mimic, the way apes are thought to copy human behaviour.

clue.text: Former railway employee is one sending goods out

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a porter carries luggage at a station

explanation.surface: A one-time station worker has gone into the overseas trade business.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter is a person or firm that ships goods abroad for sale.

clue.text: Bitter half seen in soothing surroundings

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another is placed within it
surroundings enclose whatever is placed among them

parts.note: restful means calm and soothing

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word keeps two letters and drops the other two

parts.note: taken as written, then halved to its second pair of letters

explanation.surface: A resentful half seen in calm surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept half is the back half of seen, slipped into the soothing word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resentful feels bitter about being treated unfairly.

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics
lawless means without laws or rules

explanation.surface: An ideal power that answers to no rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without a single fault or defect, which is to say perfect.

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so these letters wander out of their order

parts.note: thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Hotel owners have lost an animal that wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray cat' reads as one phrase, but stray is the anagram signal and the definition is 'cat perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with mottled black, orange and cream fur; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a cat.

indicators.note: losing its head means a word gives up its first letter

parts.note: dreading means fearing

explanation.surface: A student nervous about losing their head over revision.
explanation.walkthrough: Fearing itself would lose its F to give earing; it must first be swapped for a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a subject, in British usage, means studying it at university, as in reading law.

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered places: first, third and so on

parts.note: the first and third letters of hear
John Milton, the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: Listening to a poet strangely results in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton is Lin-Manuel Miranda's hit stage musical about the American founding father.

wordplay.note: S, E and W are compass points: south, east, west

explanation.surface: A sailor tacking, changing course three ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack suggests sailing, which fits 'directions', but here it is the needlework sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to stitch fabric loosely with long temporary stitches, a kind of sewing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a move or alteration
second meaning: a simple straight dress that hangs loosely

explanation.surface: Someone changing out of a baggy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for an alteration in position and a straight unwaisted dress.

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run on through the clue is a coincidence of the charade
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Some part of a person's foot inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot looks anatomical, but it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a twelfth of a foot in imperial measurement.

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word is judged on how it sounds

parts.note: nay is a vote against, as in the ayes and nays

explanation.surface: News that someone voted against an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying cry of a horse.

clue.text: First signs of horsefly's unwelcome, exasperating appearance

indicators.note: the first signs of words are their opening letters, one from each

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The early signs that an annoying horsefly has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hue means colour, and by extension the look or aspect of something, its outward appearance.

clue.text: Rotten team not in position to score

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A poor football team keeps getting caught out of position.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a player offside is illegally ahead of the ball and so cannot legally score.

clue.text: Cornered brick carrier holding returned chicken product

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a hod is a builder's trough on a pole for carrying bricks

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: chickens produce eggs

explanation.surface: A builder's labourer brings back an egg in his hod.
explanation.definitionFit: To hog something is to keep it greedily for oneself, so hogged means monopolised, as in cornering a market.

clue.text: Lily left books with you and me

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
us is the pronoun for you and me together
joins the last piece on

explanation.surface: Someone called Lily left some books for the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily reads as a woman's name, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, the sacred flower of Asian religions.
